result:
None of the three solutions gives the right value. I did not prove the result from scratch, so this rests on a consistency check and on partial recall of the literature.

**Check at h = 1.** The bound becomes |X| = (t−2)q + t for points of PG(3,q) with at most t on any plane. An ovoid has q²+1 points and at most q+1 on any plane. Setting t = q+1 gives (q−1)q + q + 1 = q²+1, so the bound is attained at t = q+1.

**Check for general h.** Take a Desarguesian spread of (h−1)-spaces in PG(4h−1,q), which corresponds to the points of PG(3,q^h). An ovoid there has q^{2h}+1 points. With t = q^h+1 the bound gives (q^h−1)q^h + q^h + 1 = q^{2h}+1, which matches the ovoid size. The natural candidate is therefore t = q^h + 1. I have not verified that the hyperplane condition holds for this spread construction. This also agrees with my recollection that the k=4, q>2 case forces t = q^h + 1.

**The three solutions.**
- Solution 1 gives q−1. This does not match the ovoid case at h = 1, which needs t = q+1.
- Solution 2 gives q^h−1. At h = 1 this is q−1, which fails for the same reason.
- Solution 3 gives q^{2h}. At h = 1 this is q², which is not q+1, and the claimed pattern q^{(k−2)h} has no support.

CHOICE: NONE
